question: What is the meaning of disposal indicator in relation to performance indicators (an interpretation of the ce performance of a product)?
data_group: performance indicators (an interpretation of the ce performance of a product)
description: The disposal indicator, referred to as "EI10," is a grading system used to assess the recycling potential of materials, ranging from grade 1 to grade 5. Grade 1 indicates a high recycling potential (75% recycling, 25% waste), while grade 5 indicates no recycling potential (0% recycling, 125% waste). This grading system is used to evaluate the environmental impact of materials at the end of their life-cycle, particularly in relation to waste generation and recycling efforts. It serves as a performance indicator for assessing the environmental performance of products, specifically focusing on the end-of-life stage and the generation of waste.

Therefore, a brief overview of the MP-method is provided in this section. 
The main difference of the previous and current research lies in the 
acquisition of required information, since for a new building the exact 
planning documentation or a BIM-model is provided, however only in 
rare cases for existing buildings. 
In general, the MP is described as a document, which displays the 
embedded materials in a building or built structure. The proposed MP- 
assessment method is building upon the disposal indicator (“EI10”), as 
well as the simplified LCA (“OI3-Index”) from the Austrian Institute for 
Building and Ecology (IBO, 2020). For both, disposal indicator, as well 
as LCA, the IBO-database “Baubook (2020) serves as basis. Within the 
assessment of the disposal indicator, grades from 1 to 5 are assigned to 
materials, depending on their recycling potential. Grade 1 stands for 
75% recycling and 25% waste, which means that 75% of the mass of a 
material (with grade 1) can be recycled and that 25% of the mass of this 
material will lead to waste at the end of its life-cycle. Grade 2 represents 
50% recycling and 50% waste, grade 3, 25% recycling and 75% waste 
and grade 4, 0% recycling and 100% waste. Grade 5 stands for 0% 
recycling and 125% waste, which means that the mass of materials that 
lead to waste is higher, than the initial mass. This additional mass can be 
seen as a surcharge for hazardous materials, which must be disposed in a 
specific way and therefore require more effort. For the generation of the
